_comment: The fixture Implementation/docs/Target.md 4.1 asks for: a place holding several tokens,
moved out of it in either order.
Example 9 never puts more than one token in a place, so its bisimilarity result says
nothing about the order problem of Plan.md 5. The first genuinely informative fixture
is a net that holds several tokens in one place, produced in different orders.
Under the bag encoding the two orders reach the same marking, so the reachability graph
is a diamond of four states. Under the list encoding of Target.md 3 they would be two
distinct states with the same underlying bag, which is exactly the refinement Plan.md 5
says nobody has proved. Keeping the fixture here means the day that backend is written
the comparison is one ltscompare away.
